stories.title: An Anthropic mathematician says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, maths' most famous problem
stories.summary: Levent Alpöge posted a note and Lean code (a language that checks every step) claiming a proof of the 1859 Riemann hypothesis, a $1 million Millennium Prize problem, and its generalised form. MIT's Andrew Sutherland compiled it and called it historic, but it isn't peer reviewed; the Clay prize needs publication and two years of scrutiny.
stories.evidence: A claim posted as Lean code; not yet peer reviewed

predictions.note: An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis; the proof, posted as Lean code, is not yet verified.

stories.title: New York surgeons did the first transplant in a trial of gene-edited pig kidneys with built-in thymus tissue
stories.summary: United Therapeutics' EXTEND trial is the first clinical trial of a pig 'thymokidney': a kidney from a pig with one gene edit, carrying pig thymus tissue meant to teach the recipient's immune system to accept it. The first transplant was at NYU Langone; six patients come first, then an independent safety review. No outcome data yet.
stories.evidence: Early trial; first patient, no results yet

stories.title: OpenAI says its models improved parts of AMD's upcoming flagship chip by up to 14%
stories.summary: OpenAI says its models rewrote circuit code for AMD flagship GPU designs, gaining up to 14% in power, performance and area on selected blocks, with Synopsys tools checking that every rewrite kept the circuit's behaviour. Some rewrites are in a design sent for manufacturing; OpenAI calls it a year of progress in under five months.

predictions.note: OpenAI says its models rewrote circuit code for AMD flagship GPU designs, up to 14% better, with some rewrites sent to manufacturing; a company claim.

stories.title: An independent tester found AI still trails people on judgement calls, like designing useful research tests
stories.summary: METR's updated 'time horizon' report adds fuzzy, judgement-heavy tasks that matter for automating AI research. Not one AI-designed evaluation was good enough for METR's own research, and models fell short of people at scoring philosophical arguments; the newest, such as Opus 5.5, reached 'borderline above the bar'. Few such tasks were tested.

predictions.note: METR found no AI-designed evaluation good enough for its own research, though the newest models are edging closer on these judgement-heavy research tasks.

stories.title: A Rutgers brain cap with an AI helper built sentences nearly twice as fast, in healthy volunteers
stories.summary: Rutgers' ChatBCI-Assist pairs a no-surgery EEG cap with a local language model that suggests words and phrases, so users pick what they mean instead of spelling every letter. Healthy volunteers got sentences across nearly twice as fast as with a standard predictive speller; trials with people with ALS are planned.

predictions.note: A no-surgery EEG cap with an AI helper let healthy volunteers get sentences across nearly twice as fast; trials with people with ALS are planned.

stories.title: In monkeys, Chinese scientists found brain cells that track the hand in 3D, which could simplify implants
stories.summary: A Chinese Academy of Sciences team recorded macaques' motor cortex during free 3D reaching and found many neurons tuned to where the hand is. Just the 17.7% of premotor neurons tracking hand position gave 94.1% of the decoding power of all recorded neurons, a shortcut for future brain-computer interfaces. Journal of Neuroscience; in monkeys.

stories.title: In a first six-person trial, stem cells put into the brain briefly improved Alzheimer's test scores
stories.summary: Neurosurgeon Christopher Duma reported a phase 1 trial at the CTAD conference: patients' own fat-derived stem cells, given through a port under the scalp. Five of six improved on a memory-and-thinking test at 12 weeks and amyloid scans fell 23.6%, but the gains faded over the year and there was no placebo group. A phase 2 trial is cleared.
stories.evidence: Early trial, 6 people, no placebo; conference

stories.title: In Sweden, an approved blood test matched a spinal tap at spotting Alzheimer's changes
stories.summary: Lund University researchers found an FDA-approved, CE-marked Alzheimer's blood test was as accurate as the established spinal fluid test, at least 90%, checked against PET scans, using the predefined cutoffs doctors actually use. It held up in a US research group, a Swedish memory clinic and Swedish primary care. Published in Nature Aging.

stories.title: Oxford's model says blood pressure pills prevent about four heart attacks or strokes per serious fall caused
stories.summary: Using 5.5 million NHS health records, Oxford researchers estimated that for every 1,000 people treated for 10 years, blood pressure drugs prevent about 8 heart attacks or strokes and cause about 2 serious falls; for frail men in their 80s, 47 vs 9. Some milder side effects were more finely balanced. A modelling study in Nature Communications.

stories.title: In Finland, a year of exercise training helped nearly half of over-70s on several fronts
stories.summary: University of Jyväskylä researchers followed 314 people over 70 through a 12-month exercise programme. On average strength, walking speed and walking endurance improved, and nearly half made meaningful gains across several measures, though responses varied widely; sticking with strength training predicted success. European Journal of Applied Physiology.

stories.title: In mice, psilocybin or ketamine cut habit-driven mistakes, a clue to how psychedelics help
stories.summary: Boston University researchers trained mice to use light cues to find a reward. After psilocybin or ketamine, the mice made fewer mistakes, leaning less on habit and more on the cues that mattered, which may explain part of the drugs' therapeutic effect. Published in Science Advances; a mouse study, not a human result.

stories.title: Across five studies, people who found their AI companion attentive and non-judgmental felt less lonely
stories.summary: Durham University Business School, with Cardiff and Manchester, ran five studies with 1,447 people in the UK and US. AI companions that felt attentive, non-judgmental and responsive went with more belonging, higher self-esteem and less loneliness. The researchers say companions should complement, not replace, people. Psychology & Marketing; associations.

stories.title: NPR reports some people struggle for months after psychedelic therapy, and trials may miss it
stories.summary: NPR heard from trial participants who had anxiety, panic attacks and long recoveries after psychedelic doses, even when their depression lifted. Researchers say serious harms seem rare in trials but are under-reported because people aren't followed long enough; Emory is tracking such cases for a year. NPR says US approval of psilocybin could come next year.
stories.evidence: News report: personal accounts and expert views

stories.title: Signal now blocks screenshots on phones to stop built-in AI agents reading private chats
stories.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots in its app on iOS 27 and Android so assistants like Siri and Gemini can't read on-screen messages. Users can switch screenshots back on, but Signal warns that exposes their chats; president Meredith Whittaker calls the fix incomplete and asks Apple, Google and Microsoft for tools to limit AI agents' access.

stories.title: An implant that runs on blood sugar brought diabetic rats' levels near normal
stories.summary: NeuroAxis uses a glucose fuel cell both to power itself and to sense blood sugar; when sugar stays high for 2.5 hours it stimulates the vagus nerve for three minutes. In type 2 diabetic rats, blood sugar came close to normal within two weeks, with better insulin sensitivity and less inflammation. Published in Nature; in rats, not people.

stories.title: In Tasmania, Incat is building three electric fast ferries with 55 megawatt-hours of batteries each
stories.summary: Incat Tasmania is building three 129 m electric catamarans for Denmark's Molslinjen, each carrying 55 MWh of AYK Energy batteries, the largest ever ordered for commercial vessels, AYK says. They're designed to carry up to 1,500 people and 500 cars at up to 40 knots on battery power; the first should enter service in early 2028.

stories.title: Delft physicists flipped the magnetic heart of a single atom, in a way theory said shouldn't happen
stories.summary: A TU Delft team led by Sander Otte used a scanning tunnelling microscope to flip the nuclear spin of single titanium-47 atoms, an effect their models said the microscope's signals shouldn't cause. Nobody knows yet how it works, but it could lead to single-atom scans and sturdier quantum bits. Published in Nature Communications.
